basis.statement: Observed choice treatment: Each team chose how heavily to use the assistant, given its experience, the project and the deadline. Observational design: back-door identification requires conditional exchangeability under the recorded graph, together with consistency, no interference and adequate overlap.
The graph “AI usage, volume and defects” (revision e52406e5) states the causes of ai_usage and bugs_per_kloc; a missing arrow claims there is no direct cause.

No unmeasured common cause of ai_usage and bugs_per_kloc remains after adjusting for team_experience, project_complexity, release_pressure. Test sensitivity to this assumption in the sensitivity chapter.
Consistency: each recorded treatment value represents one well-defined intervention, and a unit’s observed outcome equals its potential outcome under the treatment it received.
No interference: one unit’s treatment does not affect another unit’s outcome.

Adjusting for team_experience, project_complexity, release_pressure satisfies the back-door criterion for the total effect of ai_usage on bugs_per_kloc: all 5 back-door paths are blocked, and no mediator, collider or post-treatment variable is adjusted for.
code_volume_kloc is left out of the adjustment set: a mediator and a collider.
Back-door path ai_usage ← team_experience → bugs_per_kloc is blocked at team_experience.
Back-door path ai_usage ← project_complexity → bugs_per_kloc is blocked at project_complexity.
Back-door path ai_usage ← release_pressure → bugs_per_kloc is blocked at release_pressure.
Back-door path ai_usage ← project_complexity → code_volume_kloc → bugs_per_kloc is blocked at project_complexity.
Path ai_usage → code_volume_kloc ← project_complexity → bugs_per_kloc is blocked at collider code_volume_kloc, which is left alone.

caveat.consequenceIfUnmet: An ATE and an ATT answer different causal questions and cannot be substituted for one another.

caveat.requirement: On time-series rows use the HAC (Newey–West) interval; the classical interval assumes independent errors.
caveat.consequenceIfUnmet: Autocorrelated errors make the classical interval too narrow.

sources.title: A Simple, Positive Semi-definite, Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent Covariance Matrix (Newey and West, 1987)

satisfied.evidence: The prepared dataset holds independent rows, so the classical interval applies.

caveat.requirement: The HAC bandwidth is floor(4 (n/100)^(2/9)) lags, recorded with the run.
caveat.consequenceIfUnmet: A bandwidth chosen after the result changes the interval without a record.

satisfied.evidence: The run records the bandwidth from the default rule.

caveat.requirement: The coefficient is a same-period effect; lagged and cumulative effects need a time-graph estimator.
caveat.consequenceIfUnmet: A same-period coefficient is presented as the dynamic effect.
